 The Four M1 Insurance Group: Medicare beneficiaries reach midpoint of open enrollment
 Megan Huiskens , Josh Monroe 11-04-2026 at 04:00:00 PM EST | Updated 11-04-2026 at 04:45:36 PM EST Link Copied! Medicare open enrollment has reached its midway point, leaving beneficiaries with a limited window to review their health care coverage. Health insurance advisers recommend reviewing current plans before the official deadline on Dec. 7.
 Federal Medicare coverage applies to individuals ages 65 and older, but basic coverage does not cover all medical expenses. Supplemental plans can experience yearly adjustments in premiums, deductibles, physician networks and covered prescription drugs.
 To prepare for plan reviews, beneficiaries are advised to compile a clear picture of their health care needs before reaching out for assistance. Gathering information on current doctors, regular prescriptions and preferred pharmacies can help determine whether a plan remains suitable.Debbie Stroup, vice president of operations at M1 Insurance Group, emphasized the importance of examining secondary coverage during this window.
 Advertisement “Medicare is obviously a requirement if you’re 65 and older and basic Medicare doesn’t cover everything,” Stroup said. “So folks tend to get something else to kind of lay over top of that basic Medicare. And that’s the thing that we really need to take a look at. Because that plan that you put over top of it changes. So your premium might go up, your deductible might go up.”
 “Right now is the time to kind of figure out the name of the plan that you’re on,” Stroup said. “Gather all of your doctors and your prescriptions and your pharmacy and look and see if that’s the right plan for you.”
 Failing to review plan updates can lead to unexpected out-of-pocket expenses when doctor networks or prescription drug coverage change. Stroup explained how network shifts directly affect out-of-pocket costs for medical visits.
 “Let’s say you you have this plan that we talked about and you’re used to a $10 or $20 copay when you go see your doctor,” Stroup said. “And then that doctor is now not in network. And so now you go to the doctor and now it’s $200 to see a doctor and then all of those 200 add up.
 Advertisement ”Navigating multiple health care options can be intimidating, leading some beneficiaries to avoid reviewing their plans altogether. Stroup addressed common concerns about seeking assistance during the enrollment window.
 “The biggest thing is people are afraid,” Stroup said. “They’re afraid to leave what they’re comfortable with, their afraid that we are salespeople and that we’re going to force them into something else. And nothing could be further from the truth.”
 She noted that advisory services through M1 Insurance Group operate at no cost to the beneficiary, with year-round support provided to address unexpected medical bills or plan adjustments.
 “We are only here and there’s no cost for our services and we help you throughout the year as well,” Stroup said. “But we’re only here to see if you’re in that right plan. But if there’s something a little better out of all of this confusion and noise, we’re going to help you... The choice is always yours. It’s not ours. It’s yours.”
 Advertisement Stroup added that enrollment consultation services carry no financial obligation or hidden charges for patients seeking guidance.
 “There is absolutely no cost. It is completely free,” Stroup said. “There are no hidden fees or charges ever. And we’re here throughout your Medicare journey.”Understanding health insurance details can prove challenging for many individuals, making direct guidance helpful during the annual review period.
 “Think of us as your partner helping you make that decision,” Stroup said. “Medicare is very confusing and you might be a super smart person and be able to understand, you know, robotics, but Medicare let us handle that.”
 For those wishing to review their coverage options, appointments can be scheduled by phone or online.“You can give us a call,” Stroup said. “We’ll schedule an appointment with you and we’ll sit down and go over all of that with you to make sure that you’re comfortable.”
 Advertisement The Medicare open enrollment period closes on Dec. 7. Beneficiaries must complete any plan changes or new enrollments before the deadline to ensure coverage for the upcoming year.
 For more information, visit m1insurancegroup.com .
